name: IGF-1 DES
lead: IGF-1 DES, written des(1-3)IGF-1, is a truncated form of insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) lacking the first three amino acids at the N-terminus. The truncation lowers its affinity for IGF binding proteins (IGFBPs), and in laboratory assays it was more potent than full-length IGF-1 at stimulating protein synthesis in rat muscle cells [3][1].

It is a research peptide, not an approved medicine. In looksmaxxing and bodybuilding forums, users discuss injecting it locally, for example into the chin, jaw or neck, with the aim of growing muscle or reshaping features [9]. Believers cite its potency; researchers note that the supporting work is in cell cultures and animals.
No published human study has tested IGF-1 DES for muscle or facial appearance. Published work is limited to in vitro and animal studies.
infobox: Reduced binding to IGF binding proteins [1][3]
Research chemical; no approved human use

paras: A 1989 study that synthesised IGF-1 variants truncated by one to five N-terminal residues reported that des-(1-3)-IGF-1 reached a half-maximal protein-synthesis response in rat L6 myoblasts at a much lower concentration than the full-length peptide, which the authors linked to the importance of the N-terminal region [3]. A companion review discussed why some molecular variants of the IGFs are more potent on protein metabolism [6].

Researchers have used des-IGF-1 as a tool to separate IGF actions from IGFBP effects, for instance in a rat brain-injury study that examined a role for binding proteins [1]. In bovine mammary cells grown in vitro, des-3-IGF-1 stimulated proliferation more than IGF-1 or IGF-2 [2].

IGF signalling is involved in cell growth, differentiation and survival, and higher serum IGF is described as a risk factor for prostate and other cancers [4]. In a transgenic mouse model, expression of human IGF-1(des) in prostate epithelium was reported to cause hyperplastic prostate growth [4]. Another in vitro study reported that IGF-I has a dual effect on insulin release from rat pancreatic islets [5]. These are animal and laboratory findings; no human safety data for local injection exist.
No studies found. Related research on IGF-1 variants is confined to cell culture, rodent and bovine models [1][2][3][4][5].

lore.intro: On looksmax.org, IGF-1 DES appears in threads about local injection for chin, jaw and neck remodelling, in combination with growth hormone, and in stacks with topical androgens [7][8][9].

claims.claim: Injecting IGF-1 DES locally can grow the chin, mandible and neck
claims.believers: Users say its local action and potency make it suited to targeting a specific area, and discuss buying small quantities for this purpose [9].
claims.experts: No published studies have examined local injection of IGF-1 DES in humans; the available work is in cell and animal models [3][4].

claims.claim: Combining growth hormone with IGF-1 DES could help a teenager reach genetic height potential
claims.believers: A poster asked whether adding it to growth hormone would help reach genetic potential while growth plates are open, reflecting a belief that stacking raises effective IGF-1 [7].
claims.experts: No trials of IGF-1 DES for height exist. Replies in the same thread were sceptical [7].

claims.claim: Transdermal androgens plus IGF-1 DES form an effective facial remodelling stack
claims.believers: The author of one thread argues that locally absorbed androgens bind receptors in the jawline and that IGF-1 DES would add to this; he acknowledges side effects such as acne and facial hair [8].
claims.experts: No studies have tested this combination for facial structure. A commenter in the thread noted that preventing bone breakdown differs from causing bone growth [8].

card.summary: A truncated IGF-1 analogue forum users inject locally for jaw and muscle growth; only cell and animal data exist.
card.note: No human studies; IGF signalling is linked to growth of prostate and other tissues in animal work.

quick.overview:
IGF-1 DES is a shortened version of IGF-1 that binds less to carrier proteins and was more potent than IGF-1 in rat muscle cell assays. Forum users discuss injecting it into the chin, jaw or neck to build tissue.

No human study has tested it for appearance; the research is in cells and animals.
quick.mechanism: It activates IGF-1 signalling with reduced interference from IGF binding proteins, which in lab studies increases its effect on protein synthesis and cell growth.
quick.risks: No human safety data exist. Animal work reported prostate overgrowth with IGF-1(des) expression, and IGF signalling is described as a cancer-risk factor when elevated. It has no approved human use.
